📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough Adds an experimental `weed nfs` command and NFSv3 gateway over the filer, including filehandle resolution backed by a new inode→path index, a billy filesystem adapter, UDP MOUNT and Portmap responders, RPC version filtering, client allowlisting, metadata invalidation, and new integration and end-to-end test suites. ### Changes **NFSv3 Gateway Implementation** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Dependency and test harness wiring**
`go.mod`, `test/nfs/go.mod`, `test/nfs/Makefile`, `test/nfs/README.md`, `test/nfs/framework.go`, `test/nfs/basic_test.go`, `test/nfs/kernel_mount_test.go`|Adds NFS module dependencies and the standalone `test/nfs` harness files for building and running the external test suite.| |**Filer inode index and sync**
`weed/command/filer.go`, `weed/filer/filer_inode_index.go`, `weed/filer/filerstore_wrapper.go`, `weed/filer/filer_inode_index_scope_test.go`, `weed/server/nfs/index_sync.go`|Adds the opt-in inode→path KV index, command flag wiring, store bookkeeping, scope tests, and the NFS-side record synchronization helper.| |**File handles, filesystem adapter, and upload path**
`weed/server/nfs/filehandle.go`, `weed/server/nfs/filehandle_test.go`, `weed/server/nfs/filesystem.go`, `weed/server/nfs/uploader.go`, `weed/server/nfs/access.go`, `weed/server/nfs/access_test.go`, `weed/server/nfs/internal_client.go`|Defines filehandle encoding and resolution, the NFS filesystem adapter, the chunk upload abstraction, client allowlisting, and the internal gRPC filer client interface used by NFS components.| |**Mount handler and metadata invalidation**
`weed/server/nfs/handler.go`, `weed/server/nfs/metadata_follow.go`|Resolves MOUNT requests, maps file handles, reports filesystem stats, and follows metadata updates to invalidate cached chunks.| |**RPC version filter listener**
`weed/server/nfs/rpc_version_filter*.go`|Adds a listener wrapper that inspects the first RPC frame on each TCP connection and rejects unsupported NFSv4 or MOUNTv4 probes with PROG_MISMATCH.| |**UDP MOUNTv3 responder**
`weed/server/nfs/mount_udp*.go`|Adds a UDP MOUNTv3 responder that handles MOUNT_NULL, MNT, and UMNT with synthetic root and subexport resolution consistent with the TCP handler.| |**Portmap v2 responder**
`weed/server/nfs/portmap*.go`|Adds a minimal Portmap v2 responder over TCP and UDP advertising NFS and MOUNT program entries and handling PMAP_NULL, GETPORT, DUMP, SET, and UNSET procedures.| |**Server assembly and CLI**

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

body:
Thanks for putting this together — most of the restore comes back byte-identical to the pre-removal tree, which made it straightforward to review.

The one part I want to land differently is the `-nfs.inodeIndexPrefixes` filer flag: a process-global flag has to be kept identical across every filer in a cluster, and a missed one silently drops index rows. #10277 adds the same scoping through filer.conf instead — an `inode_index` location rule plus shell `nfs.enable` / `nfs.disable` that backfill and clean up the index — so filers pick it up without restarts and there is no flag to coordinate.

Once that lands, the gateway restore can drop the flag and the self-managed index writes, and check filer.conf at startup instead. I'll follow up on a rebased branch keeping your commits.

Hi @chrislusf, thanks for the review and for opening #10277 — the `filer.conf` + `nfs.enable`/`nfs.disable` approach is clearly the right call for cluster-wide consistency.

Happy to drop the flag and the self-managed index writes. Since the filer-side `inode_index` mechanism lands via #10277, I'll leave my branch as-is so your rebase stays clean — please go ahead and carry the gateway restore on top of #10277. Happy to help if you need anything from my side.
